questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in a common law country where English is the first language while traveling across the world.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: QUT paid for a taxi picking me up in the airport. During week 0 we were informed of how to join the social clubs, how medibank works etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It would have been nice with a guide on how to find classrooms, court decisions and how to use canvas in order to figure out what we had to prepare for each tutorial/lecture.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Overall pretty easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should expect the rent to be quite high.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is good opportunities to find a student accommodation but it is quite expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As far as I recall, it was quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I often had email correspondence with the host institution.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got registered to most of the classes that I wanted to register into. However, I, as an exchange student, was not able to register into some of the units and one of my units ended up being cancelled.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply as soon as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose a lot of units where the study load was quite high and included exams as well as assignments. In general the level was pretty good (not too easy or difficult).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At QUT I had both assignments and exams which makes the exams less stressful in general. As a person that struggles with dyslexia I found that QUT was better than UCPH to provide the help that I needed in order to get through my studies on the same terms as people who are not dyslexic. In addition, QUT provided several meetings with a student advisor with whom I could discuss my needs in relation to my assignments, exams, tutorials, lectures etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Torts, Contract Law, Real Property Law and Legal Research.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Overall, I would recommend all of my courses to future exchange students as they all contributed greatly to my understanding of common law and the legal methodology. However, I might consider weather or not there is another unit than Real Property Law that might be interesting as it was a challenging unit to manage while having other units that also demanded a high number of study hours per week.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to get an Australian bank account in order to get my bond back and set up a fixed rent transfer which included me paying a high amount of transfer fees.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Accommodation were more expensive than I had expected while public transport in Queensland is only 50 cents.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't have much time besides the studies to explore the clubs and I never received a response from the volley ball team at QUT so I ended up playing at UQ instead.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: leftwing/rightwing clubs, sport clubs etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend attending QUTIES' events to meet other exchange student although I mostly hung out with the people from my dorm or law school (i.e. non-exchange students).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to NZ.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and kindness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Register into units that deals with Australian law and don't worry about trying to find units that might be useful in Denmark/Europe (it's still the same methodology that you're using so it's not a waste of time to study Australian law).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Choosing units that challenged my legal methodology and legal English to a great extent and making friends with the locals.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning a new legal system and legal English while having several 3 hour exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
